title: The Milkmaid
imageDescription: A kitchen maid in a yellow bodice and blue apron pours milk from a jug into a bowl on a table with bread, lit from a window on the left.

statements.text: It's small: 45.5 × 41 cm. Most visitors expect it to be far bigger.
statements.why: Vermeer painted it around 1658, when he was in his mid-twenties. Almost all his paintings are this intimate.

statements.text: It's nearly life-size. The woman is painted at her real height.
statements.why: The whole canvas is under half a metre tall.

statements.text: Vermeer painted it straight onto a kitchen wall in Delft, and it was cut out later.
statements.why: It's oil on canvas, painted in his studio.

rounds.prompt: Look at the blue of her apron.
rounds.hint: What made a blue like this in 1658?

statements.text: It's natural ultramarine, ground from lapis lazuli mined in Afghanistan. It was one of the most expensive pigments of its time.
statements.why: Vermeer used it far more freely than most painters could afford to.

statements.text: It's woad, a cheap plant dye grown in the fields around Delft.
statements.why: Woad was used to dye cloth. The paint here is ultramarine.

statements.text: The apron was green until a restorer painted it blue in 1908.
statements.why: Scientific analysis shows the ultramarine is Vermeer's own paint.

rounds.prompt: Now the bread and basket on the table.
rounds.hint: Why does the crust seem to sparkle?

statements.text: Vermeer dabbed tiny dots of pale paint on the crust to catch the light.
statements.why: Up close the highlights break into separate dots, often called pointillé.

statements.text: Vermeer mixed ground glass into the paint so the crust would glitter.
statements.why: There's no glass. The sparkle is dots of pale paint.

statements.text: Vermeer scraped back the top layer so the pale ground shows through.
statements.why: He added pale dots on top rather than scratching down.

rounds.prompt: Down at the floor, by the wall.
rounds.hint: What was here before the foot warmer?

statements.text: Scans show he first painted a wicker laundry basket in that spot.
statements.why: He replaced it with the foot warmer, a box that held hot coals.

statements.text: Scans show he first painted a sleeping dog in that spot.
Scans show he first painted a second jug of milk in that spot.

rounds.hint: When did the Rijksmuseum buy it?

statements.why: It came from the Six family collection, with help from the Dutch state.

statements.text: The Rijksmuseum bought it in 1885, the year its building opened.
statements.why: The building opened in 1885, but the painting came in 1908.

statements.text: The Rijksmuseum bought it in 1938, just before the war.
